subproblem.title: Area Jacobian of the graph of a linear map: 1 <= J(D), and J(D) <= 1 + (e^{n/2}/2)|D|^2 when ||D|| <= 1
subproblem.statement: For all n, l and every linear map D : R^n -> R^l, let e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 (a in Fin n) be the standard basis of R^n, G the n x n Gram matrix G_ab := <D e_a, D e_b>, and J(D) := sqrt(det(I_n + G)) (the area Jacobian of v |-> (v, Dv)). Then (i) 1 <= J(D); (ii) if the operator norm satisfies ||D|| <= 1, then J(D) <= 1 + (exp(n/2)/2) |D|^2, where |D|^2 := hsNormSq D = sum_a |D e_a|^2.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (D : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ), 1 ≤ Real.sqrt (Matrix.det ((1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + Matrix.of fun a b : Fin n => inner ℝ (D (EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ))) (D (EuclideanSpace.single b (1 : ℝ))))) ∧ (‖D‖ ≤ 1 → Real.sqrt (Matrix.det ((1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + Matrix.of fun a b : Fin n => inner ℝ (D (EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ))) (D (EuclideanSpace.single b (1 : ℝ))))) ≤ 1 + Real.exp ((n : ℝ) / 2) / 2 * hsNormSq D)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Context. This is fact (Jac) of the parent proof (Simon 4.5 p. 119: 1 <= J_F <= 1 + C|grad f|^2), with the explicit constant c_n := exp(n/2)/2. The parent uses it for W = J_f theta(F) in [1, (1 + kappa)(1 + c_n|Df|^2)]; gwe_varifold_graph_transfer uses (i) to get L^n(B) <= H^n(F(B)). In Lean, J(D) is Real.sqrt (Matrix.det ((1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) + Matrix.of fun a b => inner R (D e_a) (D e_b))), where 1 is the identity matrix and + is entrywise matrix addition.

Notation. e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1, G := (<D e_a, D e_b>)_{a,b}, A := I + G (a real n x n matrix), |D|^2 := hsNormSq D = sum_a ||D e_a||^2.

1. A is symmetric. G_ab = <D e_a, D e_b> = <D e_b, D e_a> = G_ba (real_inner_comm), and I is symmetric. Over R the conjugate transpose is the transpose, so A is Hermitian (Matrix.IsHermitian).
2. Quadratic form. For c in R^n, sum_{a,b} c_a A_ab c_b = sum_a c_a^2 + sum_{a,b} c_a c_b <D e_a, D e_b> = ||c||^2 + ||D(sum_a c_a e_a)||^2 >= ||c||^2. This uses bilinearity of the inner product and linearity of D.
3. Eigenvalues are at least 1. By the spectral theorem for Hermitian matrices (Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues, eigenvectorBasis), A has real eigenvalues lambda_1, ..., lambda_n and an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors u_i with A u_i = lambda_i u_i. Step 2 with c = u_i gives lambda_i = lambda_i ||u_i||^2 = u_i^T A u_i >= ||u_i||^2 = 1. Hence lambda_i >= 1 > 0 for every i. (Equivalently, G = A - I is positive semidefinite, so its eigenvalues are >= 0, and the eigenvalues of A are 1 plus those of G.)
4. Determinant and trace. det A = prod_i lambda_i (Matrix.IsHermitian.det_eq_prod_eigenvalues) and trace A = sum_i lambda_i (Matrix.IsHermitian.trace_eq_sum_eigenvalues).
5. Part (i). Each factor lambda_i is >= 1, so det A = prod_i lambda_i >= 1. Hence J(D) = sqrt(det A) >= sqrt 1 = 1 (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt, Real.sqrt_one). No hypothesis on D is needed.
6. trace A = sum_a A_aa = sum_a (1 + <D e_a, D e_a>) = n + sum_a ||D e_a||^2 = n + |D|^2 (real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq).
7. For each i, lambda_i <= exp(lambda_i - 1) (Real.add_one_le_exp at lambda_i - 1). All factors are positive, so by Finset.prod_le_prod
 det A = prod_i lambda_i <= prod_i exp(lambda_i - 1) = exp(sum_i (lambda_i - 1)) = exp(trace A - n) = exp(|D|^2)
 (Real.exp_sum, steps 4 and 6).
8. Hence J(D) = sqrt(det A) <= sqrt(exp |D|^2) = exp(|D|^2/2), since exp |D|^2 = (exp(|D|^2/2))^2 and exp > 0.
9. Part (ii): assume ||D|| <= 1. Then ||D e_a|| <= ||D|| ||e_a|| <= 1 for each a (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm, ||e_a|| = 1). So |D|^2 = sum_a ||D e_a||^2 <= n. Put t := |D|^2/2, so 0 <= t <= n/2.
10. For t >= 0 we have exp t <= 1 + t exp t. Indeed 1 - t <= exp(-t) (Real.add_one_le_exp at -t). Multiplying by exp t > 0 gives (1 - t) exp t <= 1, i.e. exp t <= 1 + t exp t.
11. Since t >= 0 and exp t <= exp(n/2) (Real.exp_le_exp, t <= n/2), we get exp t <= 1 + t exp(n/2) = 1 + (exp(n/2)/2)|D|^2. With step 8:
 J(D) <= exp(|D|^2/2) = exp t <= 1 + (Real.exp ((n : R)/2) / 2) * hsNormSq D.
 This is part (ii).
(For n = 0 all matrices are empty, det A = 1 and |D|^2 = 0, so both parts read 1 <= 1. The argument above covers this case, since all sums are 0 and all products are 1.) QED
proof_key_steps: G = (<D e_a, D e_b>) is symmetric positive semidefinite, so A = I + G is Hermitian with x^T A x >= |x|^2.
Spectral theorem: the eigenvalues lambda_i of A are >= 1; det A = prod lambda_i, trace A = n + |D|^2.
(i) det A >= 1, so J = sqrt(det A) >= 1.
lambda_i <= exp(lambda_i - 1) gives det A <= exp(|D|^2), so J <= exp(|D|^2/2).
(ii) If ||D|| <= 1 then |D|^2 <= n. With t = |D|^2/2 in [0, n/2], exp t <= 1 + t exp t <= 1 + t exp(n/2).

subproblem.statement: For n >= 1, l, K0 >= 0 and cJ >= 0 there is C > 0 (depending only on n, l, K0, cJ) such that: let sigma > 0, kappa in [0, 1], E >= 0, h >= 0, f : R^n -> R^l 1-Lipschitz on B^n_{sigma/2}(0), and W : R^n -> R Borel with (H1) for a.e. x in B°_{3 sigma/8}(0): W(x) = 0 or 1 <= W(x) <= (1 + kappa)(1 + cJ |Df(x)|^2); (H2) L^n(B°_{3 sigma/8}(0) cap {W = 0}) <= K0 E sigma^n; (H3) int_{B°_{3 sigma/8}(0)} |Df|^2 W dx <= K0 E sigma^n (as a lintegral of ofReal(|Df|^2 W)). Then int_{B°_{3 sigma/8}(0)} |Df|^2 <= C E sigma^n, and for every C^1 compactly supported zeta with tsupport in B°_{sigma/4}(0), every M with |grad zeta| <= M, and every j in Fin l: if |int_{B°_{sigma/4}(0)} <grad f^j, grad zeta> W| <= K0 (E + h) M sigma^n then |int_{B°_{sigma/4}(0)} <grad f^j, grad zeta>| <= C (E + h + kappa sqrt(E)) M sigma^n. Here |Df|^2 = hsNormSq(fderiv R f x) and f^j = (f .)_j.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Context. This is Simon 4.5 (14)-(16) (steps 8-9 of the parent proof) in the parameter domain. W plays the role of J_F theta(F) 1_M(F), and its hypotheses are exactly what the parent derives. The parent applies it with K0 := K_b + l + 2 and cJ := exp(n/2)/2, and takes the resulting C.

Constants. omega_n := volume of the unit ball of R^n, so L^n(B°_r(0)) = omega_n r^n (EuclideanSpace.volume_ball; any bound L^n(B°_r(0)) <= c_n r^n also works). Put C_E := (1 + n) K0 and
 C := max{C_E, 2 K0 + 2 cJ C_E, sqrt(omega_n C_E), 1}.
Then C > 0. The choice of C uses only n, K0 and cJ, so C is fixed once n, l, K0 and cJ are fixed and before sigma, kappa, E, h, f and W are chosen, exactly as the quantifier order of the statement (and of the Lean type, where l is bound before the existential C) requires.

subproblem.title: Area formula for a rotated Lipschitz graph over a Borel subset of a closed ball
subproblem.statement: Let n >= 1 and l be natural numbers, q a linear isometry of R^{n+l}, K >= 0, R real, and f : R^n -> R^l K-Lipschitz on the closed ball B_R(0) (nothing is assumed off the ball). Write F(x) := q(graphPoint x (f x)) and J_f(x) := sqrt(det(I_n + (<Df(x) e_a, Df(x) e_b>)_{a,b})), with Df(x) = fderiv R f x (which is 0 where f is not differentiable) and e_a = EuclideanSpace.single a 1. Then for every Borel set A contained in B_R(0) (MeasurableSet A for Mathlib's measurable structure on R^n = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n), which is the Borel sigma-algebra; Lebesgue-measurable non-Borel sets are not covered) and every function g : R^{n+l} -> [0, infinity] (not necessarily measurable), int_{q(graph_A f)} g dH^n = int_A ofReal(J_f(x)) g(F(x)) dL^n(x), where H^n = muHE[n], L^n = volume on R^n, q(graph_A f) = q '' graphOver f A, and both sides are lower (ENNReal-valued) Lebesgue integrals.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (f : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (K : ℝ≥0) (R : ℝ), LipschitzOnWith K f (closedBall 0 R) → ∀ A : Set (Rn n), MeasurableSet A → A ⊆ closedBall 0 R → ∀ g : Amb n ℓ → ℝ≥0∞, ∫⁻ y in q '' graphOver f A, g y ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) = ∫⁻ x in A, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.det ((1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + Matrix.of fun a b : Fin n => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ))) (fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single b (1 : ℝ)))))) * g (q (graphPoint x (f x)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Context. This is the area formula of Simon Ch. 2, 3.5, for the graph map F (fact (Area) of the parent proof). It is used by the parent (L^n(A) <= H^n(F(A)) and H^n(F(Z)) = 0 for null Borel Z), by gwe_varifold_graph_transfer and by gwe_graph_tangential_estimate. Throughout, A is a Borel subset of R^n: MeasurableSet on Rn n refers to the Borel sigma-algebra (Mathlib's instance on EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) is the Borel one), and the proof below uses only that A is Borel.

Tools. The Lean proof may add the pinned import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz (the accepted sibling ted_tangent_plane_facts adds the same import). It provides:
- weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn: for a Lipschitz map Phi : E -> F between finite-dimensional real inner product spaces, a Borel set s in E (MeasurableSet s; E carries its Borel sigma-algebra) on which Phi is injective, and an arbitrary g : F -> [0, infinity],
 int_{Phi(s)} g d muHE[finrank E] = int_s ofReal(areaJacobianAt Phi x) * g(Phi x) dx;
- areaJacobianAt_nonneg;
- areaJacobianAt_sq_eq_det_gram: (areaJacobianAt Phi x)^2 = det(gram(fderiv Phi x (b a))) for every orthonormal basis b of E indexed by Fin (finrank E).
From lip_approx_graph_coordinates (GC):
- graphPoint a b - graphPoint a' b' = graphPoint (a - a') (b - b');
- ||graphPoint a b||^2 = ||a||^2 + ||b||^2.
Also, graphPoint a b = E.symm (a, b) with E := EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd (compare coordinates with Fin.addCases; an ext/simp proof). So (a, b) |-> graphPoint a b is a continuous linear isomorphism R^n x R^l -> R^{n+l}. Polarizing GC(ii) gives <graphPoint a b, graphPoint a' b'> = <a, a'> + <b, b'>.

1. Lipschitz extension. For j in Fin l, the coordinate f_j(x) := f x j satisfies |f_j x - f_j y| <= ||f x - f y|| <= K ||x - y|| on B_R(0) (|v_j| <= ||v|| in EuclideanSpace, PiLp.norm_apply_le). By McShane (LipschitzOnWith.extend_real) there are K-Lipschitz g_j : R^n -> R with g_j = f_j on B_R(0). Put f~(x) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun j => g_j x). Then f~ = f on B_R(0), and ||f~ x - f~ y|| <= sum_j |g_j x - g_j y| <= l K ||x - y||, so f~ is globally Lipschitz.
2. The extended graph map F~(x) := q(graphPoint x (f~ x)).
 - Lipschitz: by GC and since q is an isometry, ||F~ x - F~ y||^2 = ||x - y||^2 + ||f~ x - f~ y||^2 <= (1 + l^2 K^2) ||x - y||^2.
 - Injective: if F~ x = F~ y then graphPoint x (f~ x) = graphPoint y (f~ y), and the first block (E(.)).1 gives x = y.
 - Agrees with F: F~ x = F x for x in B_R(0). Hence F~ '' A = F '' A = q '' graphOver f A (graphOver f A = (fun x => graphPoint x (f x)) '' A, image_image).
3. Apply weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn to F~ with s = A and the given g. Since finrank R^n = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin),
 int_{q '' graphOver f A} g d muHE[n] = int_A ofReal(areaJacobianAt F~ x) * g(F~ x) dx = int_A ofReal(areaJacobianAt F~ x) * g(F x) dx.
 The last equality holds because F~ = F on the Borel set A (setLIntegral_congr_fun).
4. Good points. Let x be in the open ball B°_R(0) with f differentiable at x, and put D := Df(x).
 - B_R(0) is a neighbourhood of x on which F~ = F, so fderiv F~ x = fderiv F x (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
 - By the chain rule, F = q o E.symm o (y |-> (y, f y)) has derivative L v = q(graphPoint v (D v)) at x.
5. Jacobian at good points. Take the standard orthonormal basis e_a of R^n (EuclideanSpace.basisFun), reindexed by Fin (finrank R^n) = Fin n via finrank_euclideanSpace_fin. A Gram determinant is unchanged by this reindexing (Matrix.det_reindex_self).
 - By areaJacobianAt_sq_eq_det_gram, (areaJacobianAt F~ x)^2 = det(<L e_a, L e_b>)_{a,b}.
 - Since q preserves inner products, <L e_a, L e_b> = <graphPoint e_a (D e_a), graphPoint e_b (D e_b)> = <e_a, e_b> + <D e_a, D e_b> = delta_ab + <D e_a, D e_b>.
 - Hence (areaJacobianAt F~ x)^2 = det(I + (<D e_a, D e_b>)). Since areaJacobianAt >= 0, areaJacobianAt F~ x = sqrt(det(I + (<D e_a, D e_b>))) = J_f(x).
6. Bad points are null. A minus the good points is contained in (A cap sphere(0, R)) cup {x in B°_R(0) : f is not differentiable at x}.
 - The sphere is L^n-null (Measure.addHaar_sphere, n >= 1).
 - By Rademacher's theorem on a set (LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem applied to f on B_R(0)), for a.e. x in B_R(0), f is differentiable within B_R(0) at x. At an interior point this is differentiability at x (DifferentiableWithinAt.differentiableAt with closedBall_mem_nhds_of_mem). So the second set is null too.
7. By steps 5 and 6, ofReal(areaJacobianAt F~ x) * g(F x) = ofReal(J_f(x)) * g(F x) for a.e. x in A. So (setLIntegral_congr_fun_ae, A Borel) step 3 becomes
 int_{q '' graphOver f A} g d muHE[n] = int_A ofReal(J_f(x)) * g(q(graphPoint x (f x))) dx.
 This is the claim. (If R < 0 then A is empty and both sides are 0; the argument covers it.) QED
proof_key_steps: Extend f from B_R(0) to a globally Lipschitz f~ (McShane on each coordinate).
F~(x) = q(graphPoint x (f~ x)) is Lipschitz, injective, and equal to F on B_R(0).
SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn: int_{F(A)} g dH^n = int_A ofReal(areaJacobianAt F~) g(F) for Borel A and arbitrary g.
At interior differentiability points, fderiv F~ x = q o (v |-> graphPoint v (Df v)); its Gram matrix is I + (<Df e_a, Df e_b>), so areaJacobianAt = J_f.
The sphere and the non-differentiability set (Rademacher) are L^n-null, so the integrands agree a.e. on A.

subproblem.title: First variation with a vertical cylinder test field: |int (p_x e'_j).(p_x grad zeta~) dmu| <= M (sigma/4) int |H| dmu
subproblem.statement: Let n >= 1, l, U an open subset of R^{n+l}, V a rectifiable n-varifold in U with generalized mean curvature H in U (mu = V.weight, p_x = V.tangentProj x), sigma > 0 with B_sigma(0) contained in U, q a linear isometry of R^{n+l} with dist(x, T) <= sigma/16 for every x in spt V cap B_sigma(0), where T = rotatedPlane q. Let zeta : R^n -> R be C^1 with compact support and tsupport zeta contained in the open ball B°_{sigma/4}(0), let M satisfy |grad zeta| <= M everywhere, and let j be in Fin l. For x in R^{n+l} let a(x) := (EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd (q^{-1} x)).1 be the first block of q^{-1}x, e'_j := q(graphPoint 0 (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)), and g(x) := q(graphPoint (grad zeta(a(x))) 0). Then |int_{B_{sigma/2}(0)} <p_x e'_j, p_x g(x)> dmu| <= M (sigma/4) int_{B_{sigma/2}(0)} |H| dmu (Bochner integrals; no measurability of x |-> p_x is assumed, and a non-integrable integrand has integral 0 by Lean's convention).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ), V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H → ∀ σ : ℝ, 0 < σ → closedBall 0 σ ⊆ U → ∀ q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ, (∀ x ∈ V.support ∩ closedBall 0 σ, infDist x (rotatedPlane q : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ≤ σ / 16) → ∀ ζ : Rn n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → tsupport ζ ⊆ ball 0 (σ / 4) → ∀ M : ℝ, (∀ x, ‖gradient ζ x‖ ≤ M) → ∀ j : Fin ℓ, |∫ x in closedBall (0 : Amb n ℓ) (σ / 2), inner ℝ (V.tangentProj x (q (graphPoint 0 (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ))))) (V.tangentProj x (q (graphPoint (gradient ζ (EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd (q.symm x)).1) 0))) ∂V.weight| ≤ M * (σ / 4) * ∫ x in closedBall (0 : Amb n ℓ) (σ / 2), ‖H x‖ ∂V.weight
subproblem.natural_proof:
Context. This is Simon 4.5 (5), (6) and the curvature term of (8) (steps 1(a), 2 and 4(ii) of the parent proof). gwe_graph_tangential_estimate combines it with the parent's hypothesis int_{B_{sigma/2}} |H| dmu <= h sigma^{n-1}. Prerequisites:
- hsNorm_starProjection_trace_identities (PA), part (ii): ||p_{T-perp} v|| = infDist v T;
- lip_approx_graph_coordinates (GC), parts (i), (ii), (iv);
- exists_smooth_cutoff_half_ball_grad_le (CUT).

Notation. E := EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd, a(x) := (E(q^{-1} x)).1 and b(x) := (E(q^{-1} x)).2. Since graphPoint a b = E.symm (a, b) (compare coordinates with Fin.addCases), q^{-1} x = graphPoint (a x) (b x), i.e. x = q(graphPoint (a x) (b x)). The map a : R^{n+l} -> R^n is continuous linear. Put zeta~ := zeta o a, Phi(x) := <p_x e'_j, p_x g(x)>, and eps_j := EuclideanSpace.single j 1.

1. Facts about zeta.
 (i) zeta~ is C^1 (zeta is C^1, a is continuous linear).
 (ii) D zeta~(x) v = D zeta(a x)(a v) = <grad zeta(a x), a v> = <g(x), v>. Indeed, writing q^{-1} v = graphPoint (a v) (b v), we get <q(graphPoint w 0), v> = <graphPoint w 0, q^{-1} v> = <w, a v> + <0, b v> = <w, a v>.
 (iii) ||g(x)|| = ||grad zeta(a x)|| <= M (GC(ii); q is an isometry). Also M >= ||grad zeta 0|| >= 0.
 (iv) If y is not in tsupport zeta, then zeta = 0 on a neighbourhood of y and grad zeta(y) = 0 (support_fderiv_subset).
 (v) |zeta(y)| <= M sigma/4 for all y.
  - If ||y|| >= sigma/4 then y is not in tsupport zeta, so zeta(y) = 0.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Context. This is Simon 4.5 (8)-(12) on the varifold side (steps 3-5 of the parent proof). The parent transfers it to the parameter domain with (b) of gwe_varifold_graph_transfer and bounds the right side by (K_b E + E + h/4) M sigma^n. Prerequisites:
- gwe_vertical_first_variation (FV);
- gwe_graph_tilt_algebra (TA), part (b);
- gwe_lipschitz_graph_area_formula (AREA);
- lip_approx_graph_coordinates (GC).
(This derivation was checked in Lean from the frozen statements of these four declarations; only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound are used.)

Notation. mu := V.weight, F(x') := q(graphPoint x' (f x')), so Gamma = F(B_{sigma/2}) and Gamma' = F(B°_{sigma/4}). e'_j := q(graphPoint 0 (single j 1)).
 Phi(x) := <p_x e'_j, p_x q(graphPoint (grad zeta(a x)) 0)> is the integrand of FV, and phi(x) := <grad f^j(a x), grad zeta(a x)>. B := B_{sigma/2}(0) (closed ball).

1. Basic facts.
 (i) a(F x') = a(q(graphPoint x' y)) = x' (q^{-1} q = id and finAddEquivProd(graphPoint x' y) = (x', y), by coordinates).
 (ii) F is continuous on B^n_{sigma/2}: graphPoint a b = finAddEquivProd.symm (a, b) is continuous, and f is Lipschitz there.
 (iii) ||p_x v|| <= ||v|| for all x, v (p_x is a starProjection or 0).
 (iv) ||q(graphPoint w 0)|| = ||w|| and ||e'_j|| = 1 (GC(ii)).
 (v) grad zeta(y) = 0 for y outside tsupport zeta (support_fderiv_subset). M >= 0.
 Hence |Phi(x)| <= ||e'_j|| ||grad zeta(a x)|| <= M for every x.
2. Measure facts.
 (i) mu(B_sigma(0)) < infinity. By withDensity_apply and Measure.restrict_restrict it equals int_{M cap B_sigma(0)} ofReal(theta) dH^n, which is finite by V.integrableOn_mult (B_sigma(0) is compact and lies in U).
 (ii) mu((spt V)^c) = 0. spt V = U cap supp(mu), mu((supp mu)^c) = 0 (Measure.measure_compl_support), and mu(U^c) = 0 since mu << H^n restricted to the carrier, which lies in U.
 (iii) Gamma is compact (image of a compact ball under a map continuous on it), hence Borel. Gamma' = Gamma cap a^{-1}(B°_{sigma/4}(0)) by (1)(i), hence Borel.
 (iv) Gamma' lies in B. For |x'| < sigma/4: ||F x'||^2 = ||x'||^2 + ||f x'||^2 <= sigma^2/16 + sigma^2/256 <= sigma^2/4.
3. Integrability. Phi is mu-a.e. strongly measurable: it is a continuous function of (p_x, x), x |-> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable by hypothesis, and grad zeta is continuous since zeta is C^1. With |Phi| <= M and mu(B) < infinity, Phi is integrable on B (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded). Likewise x |-> |p_x - P|^2 is integrable on B_sigma(0): it is a.e. strongly measurable, and bounded by 4(n + l) since ||p_x - P|| <= 2.
4. First variation. By FV, |int_B Phi dmu| <= M (sigma/4) int_B ||H|| dmu.
5. Splitting. By integral_inter_add_sdiff (Gamma' is measurable and contained in B), int_B Phi = int_{Gamma'} Phi + int_{B \ Gamma'} Phi. Again by integral_inter_add_sdiff with the measurable set Gamma,
 int_{B \ Gamma'} Phi = int_{(B \ Gamma') cap Gamma} Phi + int_{(B \ Gamma') \ Gamma} Phi.
6. Graph points outside Gamma' contribute 0. Let x be in (B \ Gamma') cap Gamma, so x = F(x') with |x'| <= sigma/2.
 - Since x is not in Gamma', x' is not in B°_{sigma/4}, hence not in tsupport zeta.
 - By (1)(i) and (1)(v), grad zeta(a x) = grad zeta(x') = 0, so q(graphPoint 0 0) = 0 and Phi(x) = 0.
 - Hence int_{(B \ Gamma') cap Gamma} Phi = 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero).
7. Off-graph part. Since |Phi| <= M, norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const gives |int_{(B \ Gamma') \ Gamma} Phi| <= M mu((B \ Gamma') \ Gamma). Moreover (B \ Gamma') \ Gamma is contained in (B cap (spt V \ Gamma)) cup (spt V)^c, so by (2)(ii) this measure is <= mu(B cap (spt V \ Gamma)). All these measures are finite by (2)(i), so the bound holds after toReal.
8. Non-differentiability points are mu-null. Let Z := {x' in B°_{sigma/2} : f is not differentiable at x'}.
 - Z is Borel (measurableSet_of_differentiableAt). It is L^n-null by Rademacher (LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem on B^n_{sigma/2}; interior points).
 - AREA with g = 1 gives H^n(F(Z)) = int_Z J_f = 0.
 - Since mu << H^n (withDensity of a restriction), mu(F(Z)) = 0.
9. Pointwise comparison on Gamma'. For mu-a.e. x: the tangent-plane hypothesis holds at x, and x is not in F(Z). Let such an x lie in Gamma', i.e. x = F(x') with x' in B°_{sigma/4}, contained in B°_{sigma/2}.
 - Then a(x) = x', and f is differentiable at x' (otherwise x would be in F(Z)). So p_x = S.starProjection, where S := span{q(graphPoint v (Df(x') v))}.
 - ||Df(x')|| <= 1 (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitzOn, since B^n_{sigma/2} is a neighbourhood of x').
 - r := grad f^j(x') satisfies <r, v> = (Df(x') v)_j: (fun y => f y j) = (EuclideanSpace.proj j) o f has derivative (proj j) o Df(x') by the chain rule, and <(toDual)^{-1} L, v> = L v.
 - With w := grad zeta(x'), TA(b) gives |Phi(x) - phi(x)| <= |p_x - P|^2 ||w|| <= M |p_x - P|^2.
10. Integration of the comparison.
 - Phi - phi is a.e. strongly measurable (phi is Borel: gradients are Borel by measurable_fderiv, a is continuous, the inner product is continuous) and dominated on Gamma' by M |p_x - P|^2. So it is integrable on Gamma' (Integrable.mono'), and phi = Phi - (Phi - phi) is integrable on Gamma'.
 - Hence |int_{Gamma'} Phi - int_{Gamma'} phi| = |int_{Gamma'} (Phi - phi)| <= int_{Gamma'} M |p_x - P|^2 dmu <= M int_{B_sigma(0)} |p_x - P|^2 dmu, by norm_integral_le_of_norm_le and then setIntegral_mono_set (the integrand is nonnegative and Gamma' lies in B_sigma(0)).
11. Conclusion. By steps 5 and 6, int_{Gamma'} Phi = int_B Phi - int_{(B \ Gamma') \ Gamma} Phi. So
 |int_{Gamma'} phi dmu| <= |int_B Phi| + |int_{(B \ Gamma') \ Gamma} Phi| + |int_{Gamma'} Phi - int_{Gamma'} phi|
  <= M (sigma/4) int_B ||H|| dmu + M mu(B cap (spt V \ Gamma)) + M int_{B_sigma(0)} |p_x - P|^2 dmu,
 by steps 4, 7 and 10. This is the claim. QED
proof_key_steps: FV: |int_{B_{sigma/2}} Phi dmu| <= M (sigma/4) int |H| dmu for Phi = <p_x e'_j, p_x q(grad zeta(a x), 0)>.
Split B_{sigma/2} into Gamma' = F(B°_{sigma/4}), (B \ Gamma') cap Gamma (where Phi = 0, since grad zeta(a x) = 0) and (B \ Gamma') \ Gamma (where |Phi| <= M, measure <= mu(B cap (spt V \ Gamma))).
Non-differentiability points of f map to an H^n-null, hence mu-null, set (AREA + Rademacher).
mu-a.e. on Gamma', p_x is the graph plane of Df(a x), so TA(b) gives |Phi - phi| <= M |p_x - P|^2.
Integrate: |int_{Gamma'} phi| <= |int_B Phi| + |off-graph part| + M int_{B_sigma} |p_x - P|^2.

subproblem.title: Pull-back of the varifold weight to the parameter domain of a 1-Lipschitz graph
subproblem.statement: Let n >= 1, l, U a subset of R^{n+l}, V = v(M, theta) a rectifiable n-varifold in U with weight mu = V.weight = (H^n restricted to M) with density theta (M = V.carrier, theta = V.mult, H^n = muHE[n]), q a linear isometry of R^{n+l}, R real, f : R^n -> R^l 1-Lipschitz on the closed ball B_R(0) (nothing is assumed off the ball), F(x) := q(graphPoint x (f x)), and J_f(x) := sqrt(det(I_n + (<Df(x) e_a, Df(x) e_b>)_{a,b})), with Df(x) = fderiv R f x (0 where f is not differentiable) and e_a = EuclideanSpace.single a 1. Then there is a Borel function W : R^n -> [0, infinity) such that: (a) for every Borel set A contained in B_R(0) (MeasurableSet A for the Borel sigma-algebra of R^n = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n); Lebesgue-measurable non-Borel sets are not covered) and every function phi : R^{n+l} -> [0, infinity] (not necessarily measurable), int_{F(A)} phi dmu = int_A ofReal(W) phi(F) dL^n (both sides lower, ENNReal-valued Lebesgue integrals); (b) for every such Borel A and every Borel phi : R^{n+l} -> R, int_{F(A)} phi dmu = int_A W phi(F) dL^n (Bochner integrals, with Lean's convention that a non-integrable function has integral 0; the identity holds for every Borel phi, integrable or not); (c) for L^n-a.e. x in the open ball B°_R(0), W(x) = J_f(x) 1_M(F(x)) theta(F(x)); (d) for every mu-null set Z, for L^n-a.e. x in B_R(0), F(x) in Z implies W(x) = 0. (Here F(A) = q '' graphOver f A.)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (f : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (R : ℝ), LipschitzOnWith 1 f (closedBall 0 R) → ∃ W : Rn n → ℝ, Measurable W ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ W x) ∧ (∀ A : Set (Rn n), MeasurableSet A → A ⊆ closedBall 0 R → ∀ φ : Amb n ℓ → ℝ≥0∞, ∫⁻ y in q '' graphOver f A, φ y ∂V.weight = ∫⁻ x in A, ENNReal.ofReal (W x) * φ (q (graphPoint x (f x)))) ∧ (∀ A : Set (Rn n), MeasurableSet A → A ⊆ closedBall 0 R → ∀ φ : Amb n ℓ → ℝ, Measurable φ → ∫ y in q '' graphOver f A, φ y ∂V.weight = ∫ x in A, W x * φ (q (graphPoint x (f x)))) ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂(volume : Measure (Rn n)), x ∈ ball 0 R → W x = Real.sqrt (Matrix.det ((1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + Matrix.of fun a b : Fin n => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ))) (fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single b (1 : ℝ))))) * V.carrier.indicator V.mult (q (graphPoint x (f x)))) ∧ ∀ Z : Set (Amb n ℓ), V.weight Z = 0 → ∀ᵐ x ∂(volume : Measure (Rn n)), x ∈ closedBall 0 R → q (graphPoint x (f x)) ∈ Z → W x = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Context. This is the transfer formula of step 7 of the parent proof (Simon 4.5, "(12), (13) and the area formula"): mu restricted to the graph, pulled back by the graph map F, has the Borel density W = J_f theta(F) 1_M(F). The parent uses:
- (a) for the energy bound (H3);
- (b) for the weak equation (H4);
- (c) and (d) for the pointwise bounds on W (H1) and for the size of {W = 0} (H2).
Prerequisites: gwe_lipschitz_graph_area_formula (AREA, used with K = 1, for Borel subsets of B_R(0)) and gwe_graph_jacobian_bounds (JB). All sets A, B' to which (a), (b) and AREA are applied are Borel (MeasurableSet on Rn n is Borel measurability); Lusin-Souslin in (P2) needs exactly this. The Lean proof may add the pinned import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.Polish.Basic (Lusin-Souslin), as accepted siblings did.

Notation. H := muHE[n] on R^{n+l}, M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult, rho := ofReal o theta. Then mu = V.weight = (H restricted to M).withDensity rho by definition. B := B_R(0) (closed ball) and J := J_f.

0. Preliminaries.
 (P1) F is continuous on B. f is Lipschitz there, (a, b) |-> graphPoint a b = EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd.symm (a, b) is continuous, and q is continuous.
 (P1') F is injective on R^n: the first block of q^{-1} F(x), (EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd (q.symm (F x))).1, equals x.
 (P2) For a Borel set A in B, F(A) = q '' graphOver f A is Borel. This is Lusin-Souslin, MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn (R^n is Polish).
 (P3) A Borel version of F: Fh := B.piecewise F 0. It is Borel (ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise: F is continuous on the closed set B, the constant is continuous on B^c), and Fh = F on B.
 (P4) J is Borel: x |-> fderiv R f x is Borel (measurable_fderiv), and D |-> sqrt(det(I + (<D e_a, D e_b>))) is continuous (Continuous.matrix_det, continuity of entries, Real.continuous_sqrt). By JB(i), J >= 1 everywhere.
 (P5) Lower area bound: for a Borel set B' in B, L^n(B') <= H(F(B')). By AREA with g = 1, H(F(B')) = int_{B'} ofReal(J) >= int_{B'} 1 = L^n(B'), since J >= 1.
 (P6) Pull-back of H-null sets: if H(Y) = 0 then for a.e. x in B, F(x) is not in Y. Take a Borel H-null Y' containing Y (exists_measurable_superset_of_null). The set B cap Fh^{-1}(Y') is Borel and contains {x in B : F x in Y}. Its image under F lies in Y', so by (P5) its Lebesgue measure is <= H(Y') = 0.
1. A Borel version of the density. Let g := M.indicator theta : R^{n+l} -> R; g >= 0 because theta > 0 on M (V.mult_pos).
 - g is H-a.e. measurable: by aemeasurable_indicator_iff₀ (M is H-null-measurable, V.nullMeasurableSet_carrier) this reduces to theta being a.e. measurable for H restricted to M, which is V.aemeasurable_mult.
 - Let g1 be the Borel representative (AEMeasurable.mk) and g2 := max(g1, 0). Then g2 is Borel, g2 >= 0, and g2 = g H-a.e. (as g >= 0). So Y := {g2 != g} is H-null.
 - By (P6), for a.e. x in B: g2(Fh x) = g2(F x) = g(F x).   (*)
2. Definition: W(x) := J(x) * g2(Fh(x)). W is Borel (P3, P4) and W >= 0.
3. Proof of (c). By (*), for a.e. x in B (in particular a.e. on the open ball), W(x) = J(x) g(F x) = J(x) * M.indicator theta (F x).
4. Proof of (a). Fix a Borel set A in B and an arbitrary phi >= 0; S := F(A) is Borel (P2).
 4a. mu restricted to S = ((H restricted to M) restricted to S).withDensity rho (restrict_withDensity, S measurable). By lintegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul_non_measurable₀ (rho is a.e. measurable and finite), int_S phi dmu = int rho phi d((H restricted to M) restricted to S). This holds for arbitrary phi.
 4b. (H restricted to M) restricted to S = H restricted to (S cap M) = (H restricted to S) restricted to M (Measure.restrict_restrict with S measurable; Measure.restrict_restrict₀ with M null-measurable). By lintegral_indicator₀,
  int rho phi d((H restricted to S) restricted to M) = int_S M.indicator(rho phi) dH.
  Pointwise, M.indicator(rho phi)(y) = ofReal(g y) phi(y). So int_S phi dmu = int_S ofReal(g) phi dH.
 4c. Apply AREA (K = 1) to the arbitrary function y |-> ofReal(g y) phi(y):
  int_S ofReal(g) phi dH = int_A ofReal(J x) ofReal(g(F x)) phi(F x) dx.
 4d. By (*), for a.e. x in A (subset of B), ofReal(J x) ofReal(g(F x)) = ofReal(J x g2(Fh x)) = ofReal(W x) (J >= 0, ENNReal.ofReal_mul). By setLIntegral_congr_fun_ae (A Borel),
  int_{F(A)} phi dmu = int_A ofReal(W x) phi(F x) dx.
5. Proof of (d). Let mu(Z) = 0 and take a Borel mu-null Z' containing Z.
 - (a) with A = B and phi = Z'.indicator 1 gives int_B ofReal(W x) 1_{Z'}(F x) dx = int_{F(B)} 1_{Z'} dmu = (mu restricted to F(B))(Z') <= mu(Z') = 0.
 - On B the integrand equals the Borel function x |-> ofReal(W x) 1_{Z'}(Fh x) (setLIntegral_congr_fun). By lintegral_eq_zero_iff it vanishes a.e. on B.
 - So for a.e. x in B: if F(x) in Z, then Fh x = F x is in Z' and ofReal(W x) = 0, hence W x <= 0, hence W x = 0 since W >= 0.
6. Proof of (b). Fix a Borel set A in B and a Borel phi : R^{n+l} -> R.
 6a. Pushforward identity. mu restricted to F(A) = Measure.map Fh nu, where nu := (L^n restricted to A).withDensity(ofReal o W).
  - For a Borel T, the left side gives int_{F(A)} T.indicator 1 dmu (lintegral_indicator_one).
  - By (a) this is int_A ofReal(W x) T.indicator 1 (F x) dx.
  - The right side gives nu(Fh^{-1} T) = int_A (Fh^{-1} T).indicator(ofReal o W) (Measure.map_apply, withDensity_apply, lintegral_indicator).
  - The two integrands agree on A, because Fh = F on A. Conclude by Measure.ext.
 6b. Hence, by integral_map (Fh is measurable, phi is Borel) and integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul (ofReal o W is Borel and finite),
  int_{F(A)} phi dmu = int phi(Fh) dnu = int_A (ofReal(W x)).toReal phi(Fh x) dx = int_A W(x) phi(F x) dx,
  using toReal(ofReal W) = W (W >= 0) and Fh = F on A (setIntegral_congr_fun). Neither integral_map nor integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul assumes integrability (each is an identity of Bochner integrals in Lean's convention), so (b) holds for every Borel phi.
7. W from step 2 satisfies Borel measurability, W >= 0, (a), (b), (c) and (d). QED
proof_key_steps: F(A) is Borel (Lusin-Souslin); Fh = B.piecewise F 0 is Borel and equals F on B.
AREA with g = 1 and J >= 1 give L^n(B') <= H^n(F(B')), so preimages under F of H^n-null sets are L^n-null on B.
g = 1_M theta is H^n-a.e. measurable; take a Borel g2 >= 0 with g2 = g H^n-a.e., and W := J * g2(Fh).
(a): withDensity and restriction calculus give int_{F(A)} phi dmu = int_{F(A)} ofReal(g) phi dH^n, then AREA, then g2(Fh) = g(F) a.e.
(c) from g2(Fh) = g(F) a.e.; (d) from (a) with phi = 1_{Z'} and lintegral_eq_zero_iff.
(b): the pushforward identity mu restricted to F(A) = map Fh ((L^n restricted to A).withDensity W), then integral_map and integral_withDensity.
